input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: Section 14.1 gives us a defend-and-indemnify obligation from RevMed covering its negligence, recklessness and willful misconduct and its breaches of warranties and obligations (which, read with the Section 13.4(b) compliance covenant, captures RevMed's breach of Applicable Law), and Section 14.3 supplies the standard notice, control-of-defence and cooperation procedure. However, no limb reaches Third Party claims that the licensed technology or our exercise of the licences infringes or misappropriates Third Party intellectual property, and Section 13.5 expressly disclaims any non-infringement warranty; Section 10.7 only obliges us to negotiate Third Party licences. That is the walk-away case of no Vendor IP indemnity, so the clause fails even the fallback. We target the preferred position: we add an IP infringement/misappropriation limb and an unauthorised-access/disclosure limb to Section 14.1 (with a conforming cross-reference fix) and narrow our reciprocal Section 14.2 indemnity to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law. We do not take the fallback because its 3x annual-fees super-cap would cut back an indemnity that is presently uncapped (Section 14.5 preserves indemnity claims) and "annual fees" has no counterpart in this milestone/royalty structure.

proposal.summary: Add RevMed IP-infringement and data-breach indemnity limbs to Section 14.1 and narrow Sanofi's indemnity under Section 14.2 to Sanofi-provided materials and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] RevMed's indemnity does not reach Third Party intellectual property claims and Section 13.5 disclaims any non-infringement warranty, so we have added an IP infringement/misappropriation limb and a limb for unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi data, and conformed the Section 14.1 cross-reference. Consistent with our position that our own indemnity stays narrow, we have limited Section 14.2 to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law.
